title: Are two thirds and four sixths equivalent, and why?
description: On the fraction wall, two pieces of the row of thirds and four pieces of the row of sixths are marked from the left end. The video shows that both end at the same place because each third is made of two sixths, and Keeko doubts it because four pieces seem more than two.
teaching_notes: One idea: each third is two sixths, so two thirds are four sixths and the lengths are equal. Watch for students who compare only the number of pieces and ignore their size.

source: Look at a fraction wall where 1 unit is split into halves, t
video_script.why: The child gives the reason two thirds and four sixths are equivalent: on the wall the two lengths are exactly equal.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own fraction wall, rows of thirds and sixths
video_script.anchor: the fraction wall of the book: one whole and rows of equal pieces
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says four sixths is longer because four pieces are more than two pieces. A sixth piece is only half of a third piece, so more pieces of a smaller size need not be a longer length.
video_script.payoff_line: Two thirds and four sixths are equivalent, because on the wall they are exactly the same length

final_answer.value: Yes, because on the fraction wall the length 2/3 is exactly equal to the length 4/6.
final_answer.spoken: yes, because the two lengths are exactly equal on the wall

video_script.fraction_reading: two thirds, four sixths, one third, one sixth
maths_rules: fraction wall rows of thirds and sixths, lined up from the same left end
2/3 is 2 pieces of 1/3 from the left end
4/6 is 4 pieces of 1/6 from the left end, and they end at the same marker
each 1/3 is made of 2 pieces of 1/6, so 2 thirds are 2 x 2 = 4 sixths
equal lengths mean equivalent fractions, so 2/3 = 4/6
slip: Keeko thinks 4/6 is longer because 4 pieces are more than 2 pieces; a sixth piece is half a third piece
video_script.design: One idea: the reason is that each third holds two sixths. The wall stays on screen with a guide line through the end of two thirds.
